question: Is J6R chain first-dependence only unchanged-observable repetition, and what is the exact full-public law of its previously censored matched branch?
epistemic_role: Two bounded deterministic controls of one ideal L=2 projector orbit; no noisy schedule or general kernel

physical_and_observation_contract.geometry: J6L periodic L=2 red-edge geometry, 24 blue/green sites and 108 kagome qubits
physical_and_observation_contract.initial_state: J6M compact common +1 star/triangle orbit from |0^108>
physical_and_observation_contract.first_observation: After private physical red-X chain, jointly measure every flux-free first star; full 24-bit public flux/charge/vacuum arrays only
physical_and_observation_contract.second_observation: After public action, jointly measure all residual-flux-free stars in the actual first-postselected sector; full 24-bit public arrays; no private error/support/operator labels in a record
physical_and_observation_contract.noise: ideal exact rational projectors, no stochastic histories or readout noise

matrix.structural_control: Compare exact operator equality at every first/second eligible site under partial_one and partial_two; compare full conditional second public laws, and inspect a genuinely new eligible site marginal separately from repeated-site identities. Do not call repetition transfer.
matrix.matched_chain_completion: For each of four positive first records, enumerate all 16 assignments at exactly four random second sites under matched action, retaining the full public joint law and zero-mass exclusions
matrix.independent_unit: one exact fixed state and chain; no Monte Carlo samples

acceptance: All seven hashes, J6L chain incidence, J6R input counts and unchanged old caller pass.
First and second eligible stars equal flux-free sites and commute in their actual sector; all exact rational masses are nonnegative and first/conditional-second laws normalize.
Every positive row has only the three full 24-bit public arrays and public action edge IDs; private operator/equivalence diagnostics remain outside public records.

Repeat-versus-new-site diagnostic distinguishes unchanged operator identities from any newly observed site; full second-law first dependence is reported without mechanistic or noisy-history promotion.
Matched branch closes the old censor at exactly four random second sites or fails closed; no adaptive larger support, stochastic histories, schedule arms, bootstraps, decoder comparison or threshold.
stop_rule: Fail closed on hash/incidence drift, noncommutation, negative or unnormalized mass, public/private leakage, more than two first or four second random sites, caller mutation, or CPU overrun. Do not revise the old J6R result or release five-round sampling.
